title: Compiler Hacking
concept: How to hack on the XIOM compiler — adding custom passes, contributing bug fixes, extending the type system, and building custom tooling.
why: The compiler isn't a black box. You can extend it, fix it, and customize it. Compiler hacking is the deepest form of systems programming.
syntax_ref:
# Compiler development workflow:
git clone xiom-lang/xiom && cd xiom
xiom build
xiom test
# Make changes
xiom build && xiom test  # Verify

# Custom tool:
use xiom_compiler;
let ast = Session::new().parse_file("src/main.xi");
tips: Start with simple compiler changes — a new lint rule or minor optimization — before tackling the type checker
The compiler test suite is your safety net — run `xiom test` after every change
Read existing passes before writing your own — they're the best documentation
Compiler hacking teaches you more about XIOM than any amount of application programming
common_mistakes: Changing the compiler without running the test suite — you'll break things silently
Adding optimizations without measuring performance — 'optimizations' can make code slower
Not considering edge cases — the compiler must handle ALL valid code, not just the happy path
